questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.correctAnswerText: Control line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line. It carries air to the trailer brakes. You control it with the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracts the driver.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: Low clearance underneath a vehicle causes problems when driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Raised railroad crossings are difficult to cross with a trailer that has low clearance. Long trailers and single-axle tractors are especially challenging to drive over these crossings.

questions.question: Push in the trailer air supply control to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the control to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured.
Should be stacked no more than three feet high.
Must be secured to prevent movement.
Should have the heaviest items on top.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured so it does not move during transport. Load it to keep the vehicle's weight low and evenly distributed.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer swings around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a trailer jackknife.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working.
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, you still have normal brakes to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: When starting an engine:

options.text: Warning lights turn on and then off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on and then off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers turn on briefly and then turn off. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage during a test is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi per minute.
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss limit for your vehicle. A triple combination should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Placards should be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of material is in the vehicle and warn of any hazards.

questions.question: When operating a set of triples, what should you do with the shut-off valves at the rear of the middle trailer?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them open.
questions.explanation: In a double or triple, close the shut-off valves only at the rear of the last trailer. Keep all other shut-off valves open.

questions.question: What is true about over-the-counter medication and driving?

options.text: It poses no safety risks to drivers.
Laws do not mention it regarding driving under the influence.
It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that impair driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any substance, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: When do truck rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What is the correct way to uncouple a dolly?

options.text: Unlock the pintle hook before moving the dolly out from under the rear trailer.
Move the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook.
Remove the dolly as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer. The tow bar could fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
To allow for a change in air pressure.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. If left in the system, these can damage the brakes. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
Prevents the truck from being stolen.
Prevents the driver from going too fast.
Prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: In a combination vehicle with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: Which surface provides the least traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when driving on ice that is melting. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: In very wet, freezing conditions, using the parking brake can cause it to freeze. This will prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection has how many basic steps?
questions.correctAnswerText: Seven.
questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection has seven basic steps: overview of the vehicle, engine compartment check, engine start and cab inspection, engine off and light check, walk-around inspection, signal light check, and engine start with brake check.
